Order No.03 Date: 14.11.2024
1.

The petitioner is apprehending his arrest in connection with G (Fa) Case No.141 of 2011 registered
under Sections 16(a)(i) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present case and has not committed any offence as alleged in the prosecution report, on perusal of which it will itself be evident that the co-accused-Badri Prasad is the proprietor of M/S Laxmi Food Products.
The said firm has been prosecuted with an allegation of selling misbranded sattu of 'Swastik' brand.
The petitioner has no concern with the said firm as he is neither the proprietor nor the employee of the same.
In fact, on the date of inspection, he was present there as a customer, who has been implicated in this case in a mechanical manner without making proper inquiry.
The petitioner, however, undertakes to co-operate in the trial.
Hence, he may be given the privilege of anticipatory bail.

sentences.text: 3. Learned Spl. P.P. opposes the petitioner's prayer for grant of anticipatory bail.
4. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and considering the materials available on record, I am inclined to enlarge the petitioner on anticipatory bail.

Accordingly, the petitioner, above named,
in the event of his arrest or surrender before the court below within three weeks from today, shall be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.20,000/- (Rupees Twenty Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Hazaribagh in connection with G (FA) Case No.141 of 2011 subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 482(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

(Rajesh Shankar, J.) Vikas/
